data.body:
Forensic evidence trail (2026-09-06 RCA session, debugging-protocol 4-phase):

PHASE 1 — facts
- /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports: 8 JetsamEvent reports 2026-09-05 19:27–20:56; shutdown_stall at 21:51:14 (user-observed hang → hard reboot); boot 2026-09-06 11:25.
- Every jetsam snapshot: largest process = fseventsd at 6.5–7.1M pages ×16KB ≈ 104–113GB; mds ~43GB; mds_stores grew 8→20GB across snapshots; CrowdStrike Falcon 14–16GB; copilot 9.4GB; node 3.5GB; codex 2GB. 128GB host fully committed, free pages ~13k.
- Precursor diags on the SAME boot: fseventsd cpu_resource violation Sep 1 (77% CPU avg), fseventsd disk-write violation Sep 2→3 (8.59GB file-backed dirty/24h, heaviest stack in gzwrite = its own event-log writer), total fseventsd CPU 202,099s by Sep 3.
- shutdown_stall spindump (converted): 116 python procs (95 py3.12 all <19min old = in-flight pytest run at shutdown; 21 py3.13 of which 20 were >1 day old, ~1.1GB each, main thread "last ran" up to 453,553s ago — blocked ~5.3 days after ~28min of work; parents = uv, in pairs per session epoch ⇒ MCP/gate processes surviving harness exit). 311 git procs (69 >1day old, orphaned to PPID 1, blocked in psynch_cvwait). 112× `cmd_fsmonitor__daemon` stacks with fsm_listen__loop (FSEvents listeners). Also 20 uv, 11 node, 2× CrowdStrike (23GB).

PHASE 2 — working vs failing
- ~/rebar/.git/config (shared by all 120 registered worktrees): core.fsmonitor=true, core.untrackedCache=true. No global/system/xdg config enables it; repo source contains zero fsmonitor references. Copilot CLI shells are immune (it exports GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=core.fsmonitor with empty value), which masked the setting during first readback — claude/codex/Terminal/VS Code shells all get true.
- fsmonitor--daemon.ipc sockets present in .git and in .git/worktrees/<each>/ — one daemon per worktree touched.

PHASE 3 — experiments
- Spawn proof: one `git status` in a worktree (env override removed) raised live daemon count 2→3.
- Isolated scratch repo with fsmonitor=true: daemon auto-spawned; bounded 60k-event churn cost fseventsd only +320KB RSS / +2.9 CPU-s with healthy clients — DISPROVES "modest churn alone balloons fseventsd". Scaling that CPU rate, fseventsd's observed 202,099 CPU-s implies billions of events over the boot: the necessary condition was extreme sustained volume (session logs show 27 pytest/make-verify references on Sep 5 alone, overnight autonomous orchestration, ~19.2k tests/run, PYTEST_WORKERS≥4, plus 120-worktree git churn), fanned out to ~112 fsmonitor clients + mds + CrowdStrike, with fseventsd's log writer disk-throttled (per its own violation report) — buffering until jetsam.

Observations explained
- "Terminal using excessive memory": copilot (9.4GB) and the entire agent process tree were Terminal children; Activity Monitor attributes child footprints to the parent app. Terminal itself was modest.
- Slow login after hard reboot: Spotlight reindex + fseventsd log replay + CrowdStrike rescan of the churned tree on a cold boot. Cache/keychain clearing was almost certainly irrelevant to the cause.

Open follow-up: the uv→python3.13 ~1.1GB blocked-pair leak (MCP servers/gate daemons surviving harness exit) deserves its own root-cause; worktree `debug-9ea3-mcp-leak` suggests prior awareness.
